title: SSCC — Serial Shipping Container Code
objectives: Understand SSCC via a real-life analogy
Combine SSCCs with SGTIN + EPCIS for pallet traceability

sections.markdown:
**Think of an SSCC as the vehicle registration plate for a shipping unit.**

A pallet, a container, a mixed carton, a returnable tote — anything that TRAVELS as a unit gets its own **Serial Shipping Container Code**. Each SSCC identifies exactly one physical logistics unit. Two identical pallets loaded on the same truck have different SSCCs.

- **18 digits** — extension digit + GCP + serial reference + check digit.
- **Never reused** — each SSCC is a one-time identifier for one specific logistics unit.
- **AI (00)** — barcode-encoded via Application Identifier 00; typically Code 128 or GS1-128.
- **Pallet label** — 'GS1 Logistic Label' with SSCC + destination GLN + PO number.
- **Contains SGTINs** — the pallet is made up of items with their own SGTINs; the ASN (Advance Shipping Notice) EDI message + EPCIS aggregation events tie SSCC → contained SGTINs.

**Why every warehouse / 3PL / logistics Flutter app must handle SSCC:** scanning the SSCC on a pallet retrieves the ENTIRE contents + destination + PO context in one shot — much faster than scanning every item. Ports, distribution centers, cross-docks all key their handovers on SSCC.

**SSCC (Serial Shipping Container Code)** is an 18-digit GS1 key identifying an individual logistics unit — a pallet, container, tote, or any physical shipping unit. Structure: extension digit (0-9, brand-owner choice) + GCP + serial reference + mod-10 check digit. Encoded in barcodes via **AI (00)**. Combined with SGTINs via aggregation events in EPCIS to describe pallet contents.

## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Reusing SSCCs.** GS1 requires 48 months of no reuse; many warehouses accidentally recycle. Broken trace.
**Mistake 2: Confusing SSCC with SGTIN.** SSCC = logistics unit; SGTIN = individual product. A pallet's SSCC contains many SGTINs.
**Mistake 3: Storing without leading zero.** Extension digit `0` gets dropped when SSCC treated as int.
**Mistake 4: Missing aggregation event.** Pallet ships without a prior AggregationEvent → trace can't tell what's inside. Every pack step needs one.
**Mistake 5: SSCC without a GS1 Logistic Label.** The label must include SSCC + destination GLN + PO # + weight + carrier fields. Just an SSCC is not enough for warehouse handoff.
**Mistake 6: Ignoring EDI ASN.** Advance Shipping Notice EDI message (856 in X12, DESADV in EDIFACT) references the SSCC + contained SGTINs. Both channels — barcode + EDI — must agree.
**Mistake 7: Not validating check digit on receive.** Damaged label + wrong number = wrong pallet identity. Scanner should reject.
**Mistake 8: One SSCC for multiple physical units.** Splitting a pallet mid-shipment without generating a new SSCC = trace broken.
## Best practices
**1. One SSCC per physical unit;** never reuse for 48+ months.
**2. AggregationEvent on pack, DisaggregationEvent on unpack.**
**3. TEXT 18-char storage** with check-digit validation.
**4. GS1 Logistic Label** — SSCC + GLNs + PO # + carrier fields.
**5. EDI ASN + EPCIS mirror each other** — cross-check.
**6. Analytics** — dwell time, PO cycle time keyed on SSCC.
**7. Reprint recovery** — if label damaged, generate a NEW SSCC + record parent→child link.
**8. Serial exhaustion planning** — extension digit + 10 digits = 10 billion IDs per GCP; still plan reuse policy at scale.

## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What does an SSCC identify + how is it different from a GTIN?**

**A:** SSCC identifies an INDIVIDUAL PHYSICAL LOGISTICS UNIT — one specific pallet, one specific container, one specific tote. Every pallet gets its own SSCC. GTIN identifies a product TYPE — 100 identical pallets sharing the same product mix would have 100 different SSCCs but the products inside share GTINs. **Rule:** SSCC = 'this specific box on this specific truck'; GTIN = 'this SKU.' **Contained items** — the pallet's SSCC + the items' SGTINs are linked via an EPCIS AggregationEvent (on pack) and DisaggregationEvent (on unpack). This is the backbone of pallet-scan-once workflows in warehouses.

**Q2: How is an SSCC used in a Warehouse Management System workflow?**

**A:** **(1) Pack:** items packed onto pallet; system assigns SSCC + emits AggregationEvent linking pallet to child SGTINs. **(2) Print label:** GS1 Logistic Label with SSCC barcode (AI 00) + destination GLN + PO # + carrier fields. **(3) Ship:** driver scans SSCC → ObjectEvent(shipping) with bizLocation of dispatching warehouse. **(4) Receive:** receiving warehouse scans SSCC → ObjectEvent(receiving); one scan retrieves ALL pallet contents from EPCIS repo. **(5) Put-away:** DisaggregationEvent breaks pallet into slots. **(6) Cross-dock:** SSCC ObjectEvent(inTransit) without disaggregation. **(7) Return:** SSCC referenced in return authorization. Every touchpoint keys off the SSCC — hence 'scan pallet once' becomes a huge productivity win.

**Q3: How do EDI ASN + EPCIS relate to SSCC?**

**A:** Both channels reference the SSCC. **EDI ASN** (X12 856 / EDIFACT DESADV) is the pre-shipment message sent to the receiver: 'here comes pallet SSCC X, containing items Y' — allows the receiver to pre-allocate slots + slot into their WMS before the truck arrives. **EPCIS** is the event stream: 'at time T, pallet SSCC X was packed / shipped / received / disaggregated.' EDI is one-shot notification; EPCIS is continuous event log. **Cross-check:** if a pallet arrives whose SSCC has no matching ASN, receive with caution + flag. Some warehouses gate receive on ASN match. **Modern integrations** are moving toward EPCIS as the source of truth + EDI as a legacy compatibility layer.

**Q4: What does the extension digit do + why does GS1 include it?**

**A:** The **extension digit** is the leading 0-9 in an SSCC; the brand owner assigns it freely. Purpose: gives the brand owner 10× MORE unique SSCC serials without expanding into another GCP. Effectively splits the 18-digit space into 10 sub-spaces. **How brand owners use it:** some assign per-plant (0 = Chennai plant, 1 = Delhi plant); others per shipping-type (0 = standard, 1 = returnable). Some reset the extension digit as a wrap-around when serial reference exhausts. **Not required** for uniqueness — the serial reference + GCP alone provides billions of unique IDs — but useful for splitting namespaces logically. **Interview signal:** knowing that extension digit is BRAND-OWNER-CHOSEN, not GS1-assigned.

**Q5: How would you handle a damaged / unreadable SSCC label mid-shipment?**

**A:** **(1)** Scan surrounding pallets to confirm which pallet the label was on. **(2)** Look up ASN / PO # for the shipment; find the missing pallet's expected SSCC. **(3)** Generate a REPLACEMENT SSCC + reprint label + record parent→child linkage in EPCIS (custom event or CBV extension). **(4)** ObjectEvent that references BOTH old + new SSCC for auditability. **(5)** Notify partner of SSCC change (ASN correction). **Never** just 'guess' the missing number from context; corruption there breaks trace forever. **Auditability + immutability** — original AggregationEvent isn't rewritten; new event chain layered on top.

**Q6: How would you model SSCC in a Flutter warehouse-worker app?**

**A:** **(1)** Scanner screen: scan barcode → detect AI (00) → extract 18-digit SSCC → validate. **(2)** Lookup: query local EPCIS repo (or backend cache) for the pallet's AggregationEvent → list child SGTINs. **(3)** Show pallet summary: SKU count, destination, PO #, weight. **(4)** Action buttons: Receive / Ship / Disaggregate / Split. **(5)** Offline mode: cache last-100 pallets seen; queue events for upload. **(6)** UI accessibility: giant SSCC digits (readable at arm's length); haptic + audio on scan. **(7)** Barcode + typed-entry fallback for damaged labels. **(8)** Integrate mobile_scanner or Scandit for the scan itself. Interviewer respect: full flow, not just the parser.

## Real-world usage

- **Warehouses + 3PLs** — scan-pallet-once receive.
- **Shipping carriers** — tracking numbers derived from SSCC.
- **Pharma / cold-chain** — SSCC + temperature log per pallet.
- **Retail DC** — pallet-based cross-dock.
- **NOT for** — individual items (SGTIN) or locations (GLN).

## Advanced notes

- **AI (00)** — SSCC in a GS1 element string.
- **AggregationEvent** — link SSCC to child SGTINs.
- **DisaggregationEvent** — break aggregation on unpack.
- **AI (401)** — GINC (Global Identification Number for Consignment) — links multiple SSCCs into one shipment.
- **AI (402)** — GSIN (Global Shipment Identification Number).
- **RFID EPC encoding** — 96-bit binary form of SSCC.
- **GS1 Logistic Label spec** — dimensions + zones + font sizes.
- **Reusable Transport Items (RTIs)** — GRAI (Global Returnable Asset Identifier) — different from SSCC (RTIs reused; SSCC not).
- **EDIFACT DESADV / X12 856** — ASN reference to SSCC.
- **GS1 Digital Link** for SSCC — resolves via GS1 URI syntax.
- **Local vs global uniqueness** — SSCC is globally unique because GCP is unique; even if you exhaust your serial space, extension digit gives 10× more.
- **Print quality** — Code 128 must meet ISO 15416 grade C or better for reliable scans.
